status: All21 literacy source duties have actual prepared tasks and source-attributed creator portions; no pupil/whole-topic mastery certification or DB publication.

reciprocal-message.task: Use an original shared-building problem: a partner needs to know which block to place and where. Learner gains attention by an agreed accessible cue, gives a clear message, listens to a changed partner message and replies relevantly through several exchanges. Use spoken complete ideas and a deliberately chosen short gesture sequence (show the size, indicate direction, show placement), practise it and adapt it for a different size/location. Check the partner interpretation and repair one misunderstanding. No compulsory eye contact, smiling or fixed culturally universal gesture.
reciprocal-message.positive: Own meaningful oral and non-verbal choices and relevant replies are demonstrated; repeating an adult script or watching silently alone does not establish this performance.
reciprocal-message.transfer: Change object, partner message or intended size/location and communicate the new intention.
reciprocal-message.wholeCardLimits: The movement contribution is actual own ordered expressive movement plus adaptation, not isolated copying; a listening source panel does not certify every inherited evidence exemplar. No belief or diagnosis is inferred from gaze.

new-vocabulary-and-parts.task: Teach observe, damp and gigantic through concrete/supplied examples. Child asks about an unfamiliar use, connects it to a known meaning, then uses a taught word in a different spoken context and a simple chosen written/dictated message. Use the actual play/plays/played/playing and cup/cups/bag/bags packets to show shared meaning and changes; compare pack/unpack. Work orally first, with print available as support. Do not require a complete later derivational/Greek-root repertoire.
new-vocabulary-and-parts.positive: A new use fits its context and a word-part change is related to meaning; merely echoing a word or repeating its spelling is insufficient.
new-vocabulary-and-parts.transfer: Use a fresh familiar base or changed context and explain the supported meaning; do not assume any invented word with an affix is a real standard word.
new-vocabulary-and-parts.wholeCardLimits: Broader printed word-family and spelling inventories remain separately assessed. Source progression does not imply mastery of every suffix or written affix rule.

letters-and-formation.task: Provide all26English uppercase/lowercase forms in shuffled and alphabetic arrangements. Ask for names in both arrangements, match cases, and distinguish names from speech sounds. Model starting point, direction and path, then have the learner actually form upper/lowercase examples across the alphabet with appropriate support and revisit independently. Use accessible writing tools and actual learner-controlled strokes; typing or an adult tracing everything does not prove formation. Record readiness/support across the two-year programme rather than impose an identical age-four deadline.
letters-and-formation.positive: Naming works beyond the alphabet song, and actual distinguishable letter forms use learned movement paths.
letters-and-formation.transfer: Change order, selected letter or writing surface and retain its identity/formation.
letters-and-formation.wholeCardLimits: Comfortable functional access supports the source duty; a particular tripod posture or uniform size is not an extra Kindergarten requirement. Existing whole-card inventories remain unchanged.

phonemes-and-written-words.task: Use spoken words with two/three phonemes before more complex ones. Without print or answer pictures, isolate first/final/medial sounds with appropriate prompts, combine separately sounded phonemes and segment a whole word. Then use a declared actually taught English consonant/short-vowel and common digraph packet for reading and spelling the example words, followed by fresh words made from the same taught correspondences. Include actual writing/letter selection for each heard sound and independent print-to-sound blending. For each selected correspondence, teach sound-to-written-form AND written-form-to-sound in words; include the source-supported ch/ck/sh/th/wh and voiced/unvoiced s contexts where appropriate. The actual chosen inventory must be recorded before tasks, not fabricated afterwards.
phonemes-and-written-words.positive: The child uses the appropriate phoneme/grapheme relation to decode and encode a new regular word; reciting letter names or copying a pictured answer is insufficient.
phonemes-and-written-words.transfer: Change one taught sound or word and perform the new decoding/encoding without its answer image.
phonemes-and-written-words.wholeCardLimits: Applicable taught correspondences and segmenting matter, but a successful CVC spelling task does not certify all40+phonemes, long-vowel spelling conventions, the full phonics terminology inventory or every onset/rime/manipulation task. No source-level whole-topic mastery inference.

short-sentence-fluency.task: Use the actual original bagStory fixture after explicitly teaching its correspondence/word parts and background meaning. Learner reads the short sentences, answers the three meaning checks, then rereads to develop smoother pacing/expression while retaining accuracy. Record actual errors/support and meaningful improvement; use another text built from the same taught inventory to avoid a memorised recital. No whole-word silhouette memorisation or compulsory fixed words-per-minute threshold.
short-sentence-fluency.positive: Reading and understanding are both present, including a changed sentence or fresh matched text.
short-sentence-fluency.transfer: For example change the cup location and ask a new question whose answer must come from the changed print.
short-sentence-fluency.wholeCardLimits: The existing whole fluency claim has its own accuracy/rereading/text breadth criteria. This source task does not claim the full20–30word sight bank or all-English-phoneme prerequisite was assessed.

diverse-text-experience.task: Across actual story, information, instruction and poetic/illustrated texts, state a purpose for choosing a text, apply word/sentence/punctuation knowledge, read an appropriately matched simple passage, and discuss a more demanding passage read aloud by an adult. Before revealing a next section, record a reasoned prediction; afterwards revise it using evidence. Explain an illustration/text relation and a connection to another text, a supplied experience or the world. Share an own thought or feeling and respond to another view; neutral/negative responses are valid, and no private family disclosure is required. The actual portfolio must include verified diverse Canadian and First Nations, Métis and Inuit creator works, not invented authentic testimony or a publisher synopsis standing in for the work. Use the exact selected Van Camp opening excerpt, Flett interview portion and complete attributed Ashevak visual work in the creator portfolio. The official definition includes visual texts; this does not replace the independently read simple written passage. For the read-aloud choose the Flett information portion only after checking that its language is beyond this learner’s independent reading; discuss actual details and invite clarification. If independently readable already, that portion cannot certify the separate beyond-independent-reading claim. Pair the original bag story with the actual original bag picture: the yellow star is a visible added detail absent from the sentences. Withhold the next bag-story sentence or owl image before a reasoned prediction, then reveal and revise; no guessing an author’s private intention. Compare the actual original classInvitation, classMessage and bagStory: invite/persuade, instruct and tell a story are distinct purposes, not labels inferred from a cover alone.
diverse-text-experience.positive: Responses refer to the actual supplied material, with genuine reading/listening, prediction before evidence and own connections rather than a generic answer bank.
diverse-text-experience.transfer: Use a fresh declared work and explain which background or textual evidence supports the response.
diverse-text-experience.wholeCardLimits: Generic comprehension operations do not by themselves meet the required creator/text variety. A read-aloud does not replace the separate actual simple-text reading duty. No personal feelings are scored as moral correctness.
diverse-text-experience.resourceBoundary: Read/view only the identified portions. The Little You opening is a short poem excerpt, not the complete book; the Flett interview is an information text, not the Birdsong story. The museum work is a visual text, not a generic Indigenous story. No invented plot, cultural interpretation or identity testimony. Actual independently read fiction/instructions, spoken poetry, information and visual work collectively provide variety.

simple-multimodal-writing.task: Provide an actual classroom reference set: alphabet/case cards, taught correspondence examples and a short relevant word list. Child chooses a purpose and audience, plans a simple original message such as a bag label/invitation or an observation, and makes own meaningful letters/words or a sentence together with a picture/symbol. Have a recipient interpret it; change one unclear part and share the result. Actually consult an appropriate reference when needed and explain its use. Record accessible input/dictation support separately from handwriting evidence; a ready-made copied label or an adult-composed message is not own composition. The prepared reference set contains all upper/lowercase forms, the declared sound-spelling packet and the actual words bag, cup, mat, red, Sam, in, on, has, a, the, is. Invite an own short message and picture for a real recipient; these examples are resources, not a script to copy. Preserve the older full multimodal publishing inventory as a separate assessment.
simple-multimodal-writing.positive: Text and image/symbol choices communicate the learner intention to an actual recipient, and the reference is used to support creation rather than merely displayed.
simple-multimodal-writing.transfer: Change purpose, recipient or message and choose/adapt a resource appropriately.
simple-multimodal-writing.wholeCardLimits: A brief source task does not certify the entire older multimodal publishing repertoire, paragraph organisation or technical writing vocabulary. A reference tool is a performance/resource condition, not a new mastery topic.

inventoryBeforeTask.adultSoundKey: local short-o in dog/box; retain the learner’s accent

inventoryLimits: Adult confirms actual spoken forms before teaching and assessment. IPA/terms are an adult key, not a child vocabulary test.
qu and x can represent more than one phoneme: never equate one written letter or grapheme with exactly one sound. These contexts are taught explicitly.

This declared common consonant/short-vowel/digraph packet is not the complete English correspondence inventory or a long-vowel mastery claim. ck occurs in suitable word-final contexts, not an invented universal interchangeable initial spelling.
wh merger and short-o/r variants follow actual language use rather than rewarding imitation of one accent.

oralOnly.setup: No print, letter names or answer pictures; adult gives separated actual phonemes without added schwa. Segment whole spoken words before displaying their spelling.
oralOnly.limits: Two/three-phoneme probes do not establish every longer cluster/manipulation operation in a broader existing claim.

readAndSpell.delivery: Keep cold words unseen until the first relevant attempt. Dictate spelling without displayed answer or answer picture; print-to-sound reading precedes any sounded model. Track taught correspondences/support separately. Use a different equivalent packet after teaching a formerly cold word.
readAndSpell.morphology: For the orally taught play family distinguish root meaning and ending changes; it is not a decodability claim for this short-vowel packet.
readAndSpell.reviewCorrection: Rejected then because it needs a not-yet-declared voiced-th correspondence; selected thick instead. The separate story explicitly teaches the voiced-th in the.

commonUnexpectedParts.adultSetup: Teach the actual weak/strong spoken forms used in the sentence; do not force a short-a reading everywhere.
Explicitly teach its voiced th and local unstressed/stressed vowel before the story; this adds the needed text correspondence without declaring all th spellings mastered.
Use short i and explicitly taught voiced s.
Use h, short a and explicitly taught voiced s.

sentences: The cup is in the bag.
Sam can sit on the mat.

meaningChecks.question: Is the bag blue? Show the print supporting the answer.

coldTransfer.title: The cup and the mat
sentences: The cup is on the mat.
The bag is in the shed.

meaningChecks.question: Where is the cup?
meaningChecks.answer: On the mat, unlike in the practice story.

matchedTexts.fluencyDelivery: Read with meaning, record errors/support, reread for smoother pacing and expression, then use the unseen changed text. No compulsory WPM or whole20–30word sight-bank inference.

bagStory.title: Sam and the red bag
body: The cup is in the bag.
Sam can sit on the mat.
meaningChecks: Is the bag blue? Which words support your answer?
bagStory.status: Original invented practice text, not an authentic Indigenous text.

seedInformation.title: A seed grows
body: A seed can grow into a plant.
A plant needs suitable water and light as it grows.
Different plants can need different amounts.
seedInformation.use: Adult-read information passage with an actual safely grown plant or attributed dated record, not an independently decodable word list.
seedInformation.status: Original practice explanation; no claim that a dry seed needs light to germinate or that every species has identical needs.

classMessage.title: Tell the next group
body: Put the red bag on the mat.
Put the cup in the bag.
classMessage.use: Read aloud as an instruction text; compare its purpose with the story and information passage.

explicitlyTaughtWordParts: The usual parts of a, the, is and has are sounded through; teach their unexpected/common spoken correspondences explicitly in the selected accent. These four words are not a claim that a whole20–30word sight inventory was assessed.

classInvitation.title: Join our block display
body: Come and see our block display.
You can look at the bridge and try a safe route with us.
classInvitation.use: Original adult-supported persuasive invitation. Compare its purpose with the story, instructions and information; no claim that it is independently decodable from the short-vowel packet.

observedDetails: Blue cup partly inside the bag
Yellow star on the bag not stated in the practice text
original-story-picture.task: Read the practice sentences before discussing what the actual picture confirms and what extra information it supplies. Do not treat the picture as the answer key for independent word decoding.

officialTextDefinition.use: The linked official glossary includes visual, oral, print and digital meaning-bearing forms; the curriculum does not limit this requirement to complete books.

works.creator: Richard Van Camp
works.identity: Tłı̨chǫ author from Fort Smith, Northwest Territories, Canada
works.title: Little You — publisher opening excerpt only

works.credit: Written by Richard Van Camp; illustrated by Julie Flett. The selected text does not assert access to the complete illustrations.
works.task: Adult reads the actual linked opening excerpt; discuss who is addressed, one detail supported by the words and the effect or own response. Do not infer later events or a complete narrative.

works.creator: Julie Flett
works.identity: Cree-Métis Canadian author, illustrator and artist based in Vancouver
works.title: An Interview with Julie Flett
works.portion: First answer: the initial walk, house, trees, snowdrops and meeting a neighbour. Stop before later grief discussion; no Birdsong plot or complete-book claim.
works.task: Adult reads the selected actual first answer. Ask where an idea came from and which supplied detail supports the answer. Connect an observation to the original seed information passage or a neutral supplied garden experience. Check actual language demand before using it for beyond-independent-reading listening.

works.creator: Kenojuak Ashevak
works.identity: Inuk artist associated with Kinngait, Nunavut, Canada
works.title: The Enchanted Owl
works.portion: Complete museum-displayed 1960 stonecut image, personally viewed; link only, image not redistributed in this repository.
works.credit: Artist Kenojuak Ashevak; printmaker Eegyvudluk Pootoogook; printer Iyola Kingwatsiak, as credited by the museum.
works.task: Before revealing the image, use its title and known owl information for a reasoned prediction. Reveal the actual image and compare with visible rounded eyes and long coloured feather forms. Explain an own response or connection, accepting neutral or differing responses. Do not supply a universal cultural meaning or invent a story.

limits: Use the linked actual works with adult preparation; if access fails, retain the creator-resource condition rather than substitute a biography or synopsis.
No reproduced third-party work, text quotation, forced family disclosure or universal cultural interpretation.
The three distinct creator identities are source-attributed; do not equate all Indigenous peoples or treat co-illustration as evidence that an unread page was reviewed.
